title: Add generator-based stream adapter and unify retry profiles across Python/TypeScript/Go
author: Lena Zhang
description:
Context and motivation: Cross-language SDK users have asked for a minimal, idiomatic bridge between generator-style streaming APIs (Python generators, TS async generators, Go channels/iterators) and the SDK retry/backoff surface. Current SDKs expose incompatible stream primitives and divergent retry parameters which makes cross-team portability and examples brittle. This PR introduces a lightweight generator-based stream adapter in each SDK and consolidates retry profile names and default parameters across Python/TypeScript/Go so examples and operator-runbooks behave consistently.

Summary of changes: Adds a generator/iterator adapter that wraps the existing streaming transport to expose an idiomatic consumer API in each language and a small compatibility shim to convert the SDK's retry presets into a shared, documented matrix. The change touches runtime shims, tests, docs, and bumps SDK client minor versions. Key goals: preserve current behavior for existing consumers, make explicit the default retry tiers (fast/standard/conservative), and improve ergonomics for generator consumers (backpressure-friendly consumption, cancelable iterators, and clearer lifecycle hooks).

Checklist: - [x] Implement generator adapter in Python/TS/Go - [x] Align retry preset names and default parameters across SDKs - [x] Add unit + integration tests for stream tear-down and reauth paths - [x] Update examples and SDK docs with migration notes - [x] Bump package versions and changelogs

Testing and validation: Added new unit tests in each SDK for chunked streaming, mid-stream credential rotation, and graceful cancellation. Local end-to-end smoke runs against staging streaming gateway (streaming-staging.redwood.ai) used a scripted producer/consumer harness to validate latency impact of the adapter (negligible) and to ensure backoff mapping does not change observed retry behavior for existing clients. CI initially reported a transient Go race in the adapter; that was fixed by switching to a non-blocking select pattern with a small buffer and adding a deterministic scheduler in the integration test harness. Final CI: all checks green.

Migration notes: Existing SDK consumers should not need to change unless they rely on internal iterator internals. The new exports are additive: - Python: redwood.streams.GeneratorAdapter (preferred) - TypeScript: redwood.streams.generatorAdapter - Go: streams.GeneratorAdapter (constructor returns typed Iterator). Retry presets: old names (fast, normal, slow) are aliased to the new canonical names (fast, standard, conservative) to avoid surprise regressions.

Why this is different from previous PRs: instead of only aligning shape or renaming a couple parameters, this PR implements an ergonomic generator surface in all three languages plus a documented canonical retry matrix. It reduces cognitive load for cross-language examples and SDK parity tests and is intentionally small and focused (no protocol changes to the streaming transport).
commits: Add PY generator adapter and tests; Add TS generator adapter and type defs; Add Go generator iterator and integration harness; Consolidate retry profile mapping and default parameters; Update docs and examples; Bump versions: py 1.12.0, ts 1.28.0, go 1.8.0; Fix go race by non-blocking select; Polish changelogs and release notes

review_comments:
Marco Ruiz: 'Thanks — big fan of the ergonomics. Please add a note about how this behaves with large prefix caching and whether the adapter can opt out of prefix aggregation.'
Lena Zhang (author): 'Added a short section in docs and a test that shows prefix caching remains active; adapter exposes opt-out flag prefix_cache=false to maintain previous semantics.'
Asha Patel: 'TS types look good, but can we avoid forcing consumers to import the internal transport type? Introduced a small wrapper in generatorAdapter.ts to accept the public client only.'
Tom Briggs: 'Found a flaky race in the go integration — saw it locally and in CI. Replaced the blocking channel send with a select w/ default and added a small buffer. Re-ran CI and it stabilized.'
Lena Zhang: 'Addressed comments, pushed fixes and expanded the integration test to exercise mid-stream token rotation. Thank you reviewers.'
